mainTopic: The ban on being present during the כהן גדול's service inside, why the verse centers on the incense, and רבי אלעזר's rule on leaving the area between the אולם and the מזבח
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא on the פסוק that says no one may be in the אהל מועד while the כהן גדול goes in to atone on יום כיפור (ויקרא ט״ז:י״ז). Each phrase of the verse sets the limits of the ban. It covers only the היכל, not the עזרה. It applies in the desert משכן, in שילה, and in the בית המקדש. It applies during both the incense and the blood services, from his entering until he leaves. The end of the verse teaches the order of atonement: himself, his household, the כהנים, then all of ישראל. The גמרא then explains why the verse is mainly about the incense: only the incense atones equally for everyone. It adds that incense atones for לשון הרע, because something done in secret atones for a sin done in secret. Next, רבי אלעזר limits a משנה. People leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח only for the daily incense in the היכל, not for the incense in the קודש הקדשים. The גמרא challenges him from a ברייתא of רבי יוסי and defends him by reading that ברייתא narrowly. The final answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ban applies in the sanctuary, not the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules out the idea that people must leave the עזרה. The words 'באהל מועד' limit the ban to the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think people may not be present even in the Courtyard. So the verse says 'in the Tent of Meeting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues explaining the verse that bans people from being inside while the כהן גדול serves. Here it sets a limit on where the ban applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the verse says 'no person shall be,' one might think the whole Temple area must be empty, even the עזרה. The words 'באהל מועד' point to the sanctuary building itself, the היכל. So the ban covers only that building, not the open courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think' — introduces a possible but wrong assumption
The Temple Courtyard, the open area outside the sanctuary building
'The verse teaches' — introduces the proof from a פסוק
Tent of Meeting; here it means the sanctuary building (היכל)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of the ברייתא. Its opening (the words 'וכל אדם לא יהיה') came on the previous amud. 'יכול אפילו בעזרה' is a limit on that earlier rule.

phrases.english: One might think the ban applies even in the Courtyard —
phrases.notes: A possible assumption the ברייתא will reject

phrases.english: therefore the verse says: 'in the Tent of Meeting.'
phrases.notes: This limits the ban to the sanctuary building

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on being present applies to the היכל, not to the עזרה.

steps.title: The ban also applies in Shiloh and the Temple
steps.stepSummary: 'אהל מועד' might mean only the desert משכן. The word 'בקודש' widens the ban to שילה and the בית עולמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this about the Tent of Meeting in the desert. How do I know it applies to שילה and the בית עולמים? The verse says 'in the Holy place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the ban only applied to the desert משכן. It answers from the word 'בקודש' that it applies to every sanctuary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אהל מועד' literally describes the tent in the desert, so it might seem limited to that one time and place. The general word 'בקודש' (in the holy place) covers any holy sanctuary. That includes the משכן at שילה and the בית המקדש in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only have' — what the verse teaches so far, before widening it
Shiloh, where the משכן stood for many years in ארץ ישראל
'The Eternal House' — the בית המקדש in ירושלים
'From where do we know?' — asks for a source

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: I only know this about the Tent of Meeting in the desert;
from where do I know it for Shiloh and the Eternal House?
The verse says: 'in the Holy place.'
phrases.notes: A general word that covers any sanctuary

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the place-based rule from step 1 across different sanctuaries
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies to the desert משכן, to שילה, and to the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The ban also covers the blood sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The basic verse teaches the ban during the הקטרה. The words 'בבואו לכפר' extend it to the time of מתן דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about the time of burning the incense. How do I know it applies when the blood is sprinkled? The verse says 'when he comes to atone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now moves from place to time. It widens the ban from the incense burning to the blood sprinkling as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the main verse is about the incense service. It does not explain why yet; the גמרא will ask about this in step 6. The words 'בבואו לכפר' add the blood service, because sprinkling the blood is what brings atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the incense (קטורת) in the קודש הקדשים
Sprinkling the blood of the יום כיפורים offerings
To atone

phrases.english: I only know this for the time of the incense burning;
from where do I know it for the time of the blood sprinklings?
The verse says: 'when he comes to atone.'
phrases.notes: Atonement is done through the blood

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from widening the place to widening the time
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies during the blood sprinklings as well as during the incense burning.

steps.title: The ban lasts until he comes out
steps.stepSummary: The words 'עד צאתו' extend the ban from his entering until his leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about when he enters. How do I know it applies until he leaves? The verse says 'until he comes out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא makes one more time-based extension. The ban starts when he goes in and lasts until he walks out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בבואו' could mean only the moment of entering. 'עד צאתו' shows the ban continues through his whole stay inside, including his exit.

keyTerms.meaning: His entering
His leaving
'Until he comes out'

phrases.english: I only know this for his entering;
from where do I know it for his leaving?
The verse says: 'until he comes out.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the time-based widening from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban stays in force from his entering until his leaving.

steps.title: The order of atonement
steps.stepSummary: From the order of the verse's last phrase, the ברייתא learns a sequence of atonement. The כהן גדול comes first, then his household, then the כהנים, then all of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall atone for himself, for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel.' His atonement comes before his household's. His household's comes before that of his fellow priests. His fellow priests' comes before that of all Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining the end of the verse. The order of the words teaches the order of atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse lists 'himself, his household, all Israel,' and the ברייתא reads that list as a fixed sequence. It also places 'his brothers the כהנים' between his household and ישראל. The idea is that one must first be cleared of sin before atoning for others.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement
Comes before, takes priority
His brothers the priests
The whole Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is complete. The ban applies only in the היכל, in every sanctuary, during both the incense and the blood services, from his entering until his leaving. Atonement goes in order: himself, his household, the כהנים, then ישראל.

phrases.english: 'And he shall atone for himself and for his household
and for all the congregation of Israel':
his atonement comes before the atonement of his household;

phrases.aramaic: כַּפָּרַת בֵּיתוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְכַפָּרַת אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים,
phrases.english: his household's atonement comes before that of his brothers the priests;
and the atonement of his brothers the priests comes before
the atonement of all the congregation of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִפֶּר בַּעֲדוֹ וּבְעַד בֵּיתוֹ וּבְעַד כׇּל קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ban itself to the closing phrase of the same verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Atonement goes in order: the כהן גדול, his household, the כהנים, then all of ישראל.

steps.title: Why is the basic verse about the incense?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's claim that the base verse refers to the הקטרה and asks where in the verse this is implied.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'I only know about the time of burning the incense.' Where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is done, and the גמרא now begins to analyze it. It asks a clarifying question that sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse never mentions incense. Still, the ברייתא assumed it was about the הקטרה, and only added the blood service from 'בבואו לכפר.' The גמרא wants to know what in the verse points to the incense.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said' — quotes a line from the ברייתא in order to analyze it
'Where is this implied?' — asks how a reading comes out of the text

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּשְׁעַת הַקְטָרָה.
phrases.english: The Master said: 'I only know this for the time of the incense burning.'
Where is this implied?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּשְׁעַת הַקְטָרָה. מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to analyze an assumption made in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the verse shows that its basic subject is the incense burning

steps.title: Only the incense atones for everyone equally
steps.stepSummary: רבא, רבי יצחק בר אבדימי, and רבי אלעזר answer from the end of the verse. The only atonement shared equally by everyone listed is the הקטרת הקטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and so said רבי יצחק בר אבדימי, and so said רבי אלעזר: the verse says 'and he shall atone for himself, for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel.' Which atonement is the same for him, his household, his fellow priests, and all Israel? You must say it is the burning of the incense.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים give the same answer. The end of the verse describes one atonement that covers everyone, and only the incense fits that description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull's blood atones for the כהן גדול and the כהנים, and the goat's blood atones for ישראל. So neither blood atones for everyone together. The incense is one act that serves everyone equally, so the verse's main subject must be the הקטרה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse says'
That is equal or the same (for everyone)
'You must say' — the only answer that fits
The burning of the incense

steps.whatToRemember: The ban in the verse is mainly about the incense service. We know this because only the incense brings one shared atonement to the כהן גדול, his household, the כהנים, and all of ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the order of atonement in step 5. That step is about who is atoned for first. This step is about which single service atones for all of them together.

phrases.english: Rava said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי,
phrases.english: and so said Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi,
and so said Rabbi Elazar:
The verse says: 'And he shall atone for himself and for his household
and for all the congregation of Israel.'
Which atonement is the same for him and for his household
and for his brothers the priests and for all the congregation of Israel?
You must say: this is the burning of the incense.
phrases.notes: The blood offerings each atone for only some of these groups

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי, וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of the verse describes one atonement shared equally by everyone, and only the incense fits.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the end of a verse can define the subject of its beginning. It also explains why the blood service needed a separate extra source ('בבואו לכפר').

steps.title: Can incense really atone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether קטורת can actually bring atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 7 concluded that the shared atonement in the verse comes from the קטורת. Now the גמרא stops to ask whether incense atones at all. This question sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Atonement is usually connected to animal offerings and their blood. Incense is not an animal sacrifice. So the reading from Step 7 needs support showing that incense can atone.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense burned in the Temple
Brings atonement

phrases.english: And does incense bring atonement?
phrases.notes: A real question that checks the answer given in Step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basic premise behind Step 7's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there any source that incense has power to atone?

steps.title: Yes, a verse shows that incense atones
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא teaches from the story of אהרן stopping the plague that incense atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. רבי חנניא taught: We learned that incense atones, because the verse says, 'And he put on the incense and atoned for the people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes. It brings a teaching from רבי חנניא that uses a verse as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במדבר (17:12), אהרן stops the plague by offering incense. The verse then says 'ויכפר על העם', 'and he atoned for the people.' This shows directly that the incense itself brought atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Taught (introduces a ברייתא)
And he atoned for the people

phrases.english: Yes, as Rabbi Chananya taught:
We learned that incense atones,
as it says: 'And he put on the incense
phrases.notes: From the story of אהרן stopping the plague after קרח's rebellion.

phrases.english: and atoned for the people.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8 with a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Incense does atone, as the verse in במדבר 17:12 shows.

steps.title: Incense atones for לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that incense atones for לשון הרע, because a hidden act atones for a hidden sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: For what does incense atone? For לשון הרע. Let something done in secret come and atone for an act done in secret.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related teaching that says which sin incense atones for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The incense is burned privately inside the היכל, with no one else present. לשון הרע is usually spoken privately, behind a person's back. So a hidden service atones for a hidden sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study house of רבי ישמעאל
Speaking badly about others
In secret, privately

steps.whatToRemember: Incense atones. The verse about אהרן proves it, and it specifically atones for לשון הרע: something done in secret atones for a sin done in secret.

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For what does incense atone?
For evil speech.
Let something done in secret come
phrases.notes: The incense is offered privately in the היכל.

phrases.english: and atone for an act done in secret.
phrases.notes: לשון הרע is usually spoken in private.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to Step 9 by naming the specific sin incense atones for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incense atones for לשון הרע, measure for measure: a secret service for a secret sin.

steps.title: A משנה: people leave the area near the altar during incense burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח while incense is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: People leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח at the time of the incense burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a related topic by quoting a משנה from another place. It sets up רבי אלעזר's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 taught that no one may be in the אהל מועד while the כהן is inside. This משנה adds a further area people must leave during incense burning: the courtyard space between the אולם (the entrance hall) and the outer מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
They separate themselves, they leave
The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The outer altar in the courtyard
The burning (of the incense)

phrases.english: We learned there:
They leave the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar
at the time of the incense burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the verse about leaving the אהל מועד to a related משנה about leaving the area near the altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During incense burning, people must leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the משנה to incense burned in the היכל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the משנה's rule applies only to the daily incense in the היכל. When incense is burned in the קודש הקדשים, people leave only the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: They taught this only for the incense burning of the היכל. But at the incense burning inside the innermost chamber, people leave the היכל, and they do not leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר limits the משנה. He says it applies only to one kind of incense burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daily incense is burned in the היכל, so people must stay farther away, past the אולם. On יום כיפור the incense is burned in the קודש הקדשים, which is one room deeper. Then people only need to leave the היכל, and the area between the אולם and the מזבח is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of...
The Sanctuary, the room outside the קודש הקדשים
The innermost chamber, the קודש הקדשים

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards: the holier incense of יום כיפור requires people to move away less. The reason is that the incense is deeper inside, so the area that must be emptied moves inward as well.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁעַת הַקְטָרָה דְּהֵיכָל,
phrases.english: They taught this only at the incense burning of the Sanctuary,
but at the incense burning in the innermost chamber,
they leave the Sanctuary,
but they do not leave the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה quoted in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule applies only to incense in the היכל. For incense in the קודש הקדשים, people leave only the היכל.

steps.title: Objection from רבי יוסי's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה objects to רבי אלעזר from a ברייתא. רבי יוסי says people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח during incense burning, and also during certain blood offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objected (some say the objection is unattributed): רבי יוסי says, Just as people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח at the incense burning, so too they leave at the blood presentation of the פר כהן משיח, the פר העלם דבר של ציבור, and the שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: An objection to רבי אלעזר begins here. The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא, and the end of that ברייתא in the next step completes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי adds that people must also leave during the blood rites of three special offerings. The blood of these offerings is sprinkled inside the היכל. So far the ברייתא extends the rule. The point that challenges רבי אלעזר comes in the ברייתא's next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection
Some say it was said without a named author
The bull brought by the כהן גדול for a mistaken ruling
The bull brought for the community's mistake based on a mistaken ruling of the בית דין
The goats brought for the community's unintentional idol worship

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava objected,
and some say it was said unattributed:
Rabbi Yosei says:
Just as they leave the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar
at the time of the incense burning,
so too they leave at the time of the blood presentation
of the bull of the anointed priest,
and the bull for the community's unwitting sin,
and the goats for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an objection to רבי אלעזר's limitation in Step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states the rules for leaving the area between the אולם and the מזבח, and its wording, completed in the next step, does not fit רבי אלעזר's limitation.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: the area near the altar is left only during incense burning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the היכל has a stricter rule: people leave it during incense burning and also at other times. From the area between the אולם and the מזבח, people leave only during incense burning, with no limit stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what higher standard does the היכל have over the area between the אולם and the מזבח? Only this: from the היכל people leave both at the incense burning and not at the incense burning, while from the area between the אולם and the מזבח they leave only at the incense burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining how the היכל is stricter than the area near the altar. This line gives the wording the objection depends on, and the next step spells out the challenge against רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח during 'incense burning' without saying which kind. That seems to include every incense burning, even the יום כיפור incense in the קודש הקדשים. רבי אלעזר said people do not leave that area for the inner incense, so the ברייתא seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: A higher level of strictness
Both... and...
Not at the time of the incense burning (here, during the blood rites)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר limits the משנה's rule to the daily incense in the היכל. The ברייתא says 'only at the incense burning' with no limit, and this is the basis of the objection against him.

phrases.english: If so, what higher standard is there
for the Sanctuary over the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar?
Only that from the Sanctuary they leave
both at the time of the incense burning
and not at the time of the incense burning,
phrases.notes: Meaning during the blood rites of the offerings listed in Step 13.

phrases.english: while from between the Entrance Hall and the altar
they leave only at the time of the incense burning.
phrases.notes: No kind of incense burning is specified. This is the wording that challenges רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מָה מַעֲלָה יֵשׁ בֵּין הַהֵיכָל לְבֵין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 13 and gives the wording on which the objection rests.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that people do not leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח during the inner incense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'incense burning' with no limit, which seems to include the inner incense of יום כיפור and so contradicts רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא shows people leave during the incense, so maybe even the קודש הקדשים incense
steps.stepSummary: The challenge reaches its point. The ברייתא says people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח 'at the time of burning.' Doesn't that mean the incense burned in the קודש הקדשים?
steps.simpleTranslation: At least we see that at the time of burning they do leave. Isn't this talking about the burning in the innermost chamber?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge from the ברייתא. It suggests that the ברייתא's words 'at the time of burning' mean the יום כיפור incense in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said that when incense is burned in the קודש הקדשים, people leave only the היכל, not the area between the אולם and the מזבח. If the ברייתא means that people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח even for the קודש הקדשים incense, then רבי אלעזר is directly contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: At least / in any case: 'this much we can see'
They leave / move away (from the area)
'Isn't it…?': the גמרא suggests a reading it wants to prove
The innermost chamber, the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: At least at the time of burning, they do leave.
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא of רבי יוסי (steps 13-14).

phrases.english: Is it not
at the time of burning in the innermost chamber (the קודש הקדשים)?
phrases.notes: If so, this contradicts רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת הַקְטָרָה מִיהָא פָּרְשִׁי. מַאי לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from the ברייתא that was quoted in steps 13-14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that for the קודש הקדשים incense, people leave only the היכל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's unspecified 'time of burning' is read as including the קודש הקדשים incense. That would mean people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח even then, against רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא means the daily incense in the היכל
steps.stepSummary: The defense: the ברייתא's 'time of burning' means only the daily incense of the היכל, not the incense of the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means the time of burning in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. It reads the ברייתא as talking only about the daily incense in the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'time of burning' is limited to the היכל incense, the ברייתא no longer says anything about the קודש הקדשים incense. It then matches רבי אלעזר exactly: people leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח only for the daily היכל incense.

keyTerms.meaning: No: a rejection of the suggested reading
The Sanctuary, where the daily incense is burned on the golden altar

phrases.english: No,
it means at the time of burning in the היכל.
phrases.notes: This is the daily incense, which is רבי אלעזר's case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 by reading the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source (limiting its case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'time of burning' includes the קודש הקדשים incense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's 'time of burning' means only the daily incense in the היכל.

steps.title: If so, the היכל would have two higher standards, not one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the defense. If the ברייתא means only the היכל incense, there is a second difference between the two areas. People leave the היכל even for the קודש הקדשים incense, but they do not leave the outer area for it. So why does the ברייתא mention only one 'higher standard'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the ברייתא says 'what higher standard' as if there is only one. But there is another higher standard. People leave the היכל both during its own incense and during the קודש הקדשים incense. From between the אולם and the מזבח, people leave only during the היכל incense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. Reading the ברייתא that way creates a second advantage for the היכל, which the ברייתא never mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'what higher standard does the היכל have?' and lists one difference: people leave it at other times too. But under the defense's reading, there would be an extra difference. People leave the היכל for the קודש הקדשים incense, but not the outer area. A ברייתא listing the differences should have mentioned this one as well.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem caused by the previous answer
'What higher standard?': the ברייתא's wording, implying one difference
And nothing more
But there is…: points to something that was left out

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on רבי אלעזר's ruling itself. It attacks the defense's reading of the ברייתא. The problem is that the reading leaves out a difference the ברייתא should have listed.

phrases.english: If so,
the ברייתא says 'what higher standard' (one), and no more,
but there is this other higher standard:
that from the היכל they leave
both at the time of its own incense burning,
and at the time of burning in the innermost chamber,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר's own rule (step 12).

phrases.english: whereas from between the אולם and the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: לָא פָּרְשִׁי אֶלָּא בִּשְׁעַת הַקְטָרָה דְהֵיכָל!
phrases.english: they leave only at the time of burning in the היכל!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָא ״מָה מַעֲלָה״ וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא's 'time of burning' means only the daily היכל incense.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the היכל would have two higher standards, but the ברייתא's wording 'what higher standard' implies only one. So the reading seems to leave out a difference the ברייתא should have taught.

steps.title: The ברייתא already teaches that difference
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא does teach this difference. Its words 'whether at the time of burning or not at the time of burning' already include leaving the היכל at times other than the daily incense. This answer continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is exactly what it teaches: 'except that in the היכל they leave both at the time of burning and not at the time of burning, while from between the אולם and the מזבח they do not leave…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'missing' difference is not missing. It is built into the ברייתא's words 'not at the time of burning.' This answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's one 'higher standard' already covers more than one case. Leaving the היכל 'not at the time of burning' (of the היכל) includes the time when incense is burned in the קודש הקדשים. So there is no extra difference the ברייתא forgot to list, and the defense of רבי אלעזר still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it teaches': the answer is already in the source's words
Except that: introduces the היכל's extra strictness
Not at the time of the (היכל) incense burning, meaning at other times
They do not leave

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common Talmudic move. When a source seems to leave something out, the גמרא often shows that its broad wording already includes it.

phrases.english: That is what it teaches:
except that from the היכל they leave
both at the time of burning
and not at the time of burning,
phrases.notes: These are other times, beyond the daily היכל incense.

phrases.english: while from between the אולם and the מזבח they do not leave
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17 by showing the ברייתא already contains the difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source's own wording already includes the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists only one higher standard and leaves out the difference about the קודש הקדשים incense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'and not at the time of burning' already include that difference, so nothing is missing.
